text: What is the key characteristic that distinguishes a public cloud from a private cloud?
options: A public cloud is accessed over the internet and a private cloud is not.
A public cloud is available to anyone who purchases the service; a private cloud is used by a single organisation.
A public cloud is hosted off site and a private cloud is hosted on site.
A public cloud is always cheaper than a private cloud.
explanation: General availability to anyone who buys the service is what defines a public cloud. A private cloud is defined by being used by a single organisation, regardless of whether it is hosted on-site or off-site.

text: In the shared responsibility model, which of the following areas remains with the customer across on-premises, IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS?
explanation: Identities and users, customer data, and configurations/settings are the three areas that never transfer to the provider. They remain the customer's responsibility in every cloud model.

text: An organisation moves a workload from its own datacentre to Azure Virtual Machines (IaaS). Which responsibility transfers to Microsoft?
options: Patching the operating system on the virtual machine
Classifying and protecting the data stored on the virtual machine
Managing which users have access to the virtual machine
Physical security of the datacentre housing the hardware
explanation: In Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), the provider (Microsoft) takes over the physical layer: physical hosts, physical network, and physical datacentre. The customer retains the OS, data, and access controls.

text: An organisation uses its own datacentre for patient records and Azure for its public website, with the two environments interconnected. Which cloud model is this?
explanation: A hybrid cloud is an interconnected computing environment that uses both public (Azure) and private (own datacentre) clouds together.
